title: As a massive fan of Immersive Theatre, I simply had to check out #Vio...
transcript: A play with no live actors, where you are walking barefoot through a series of dark and dimly lit corridors, guided only by light. That is the premise for Viola's Room, which is a new show by Punchdrunk, the team behind Sleep No More. Although unlike sleep no more, this one does have a much clearer narrative, as throughout the experience you are listening to what is essentially a bedtime story through a pair of headphones. Although in typical Punchdrunk fashion, it is very much up for interpretation. And there were certainly moments where I was like, this is really cool. I'm vibing with it, but I don't really know what's going on. It's definitely more coherent than something like sleep no more, but it is still very abstract and very out there. As for the experience itself, it's definitely very cool. I've certainly never experienced anything like it. Like I said at the beginning, you are barefoot throughout the experience. That's gonna be a deal breaker for some people, and while I personally didn't mind it, I'm also not entirely sure how much it really added to the experience. There are different textures on the ground throughout the experience, and it does somewhat inform the journey, but ultimately, I probably could have done without it. The environments themselves are very well done. Punchdrunk always has a really great attention to detail, and this is definitely no exception. Some of the sets are more detailed than others, and that's definitely Intentional, but when you do get into those more detailed rooms, I definitely recommend paying attention to your surroundings as there are certain props that will pop up again and again throughout the experience. And there's definitely a lot of symbolism to be found in each of their appearances, so be on the lookout. There's definitely a ton of trigger warnings for this thing. There are times when it is completely pitch black or very, very dimly lit to the point where you can only see like directly in front of you. There are times when it gets really tight and could trigger some claustrophobia, so if you have any specific questions about that kind of stuff, I'm happy to answer in the comments. But all in all, would I recommend Viola's room? Yes, I would. It is just such a unique experience, and while it lacks the free exploration or scale of something like Sleep No More, it can still be rewarding in its own ways and will leave you with a ton to dissect after the fact.
